original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Every ordered pair of one-transvection charts at two of the 184 retained-center contacts strictly raises the paid r^theta moment for every theta in (0,1). Edgeless sets add. No selected-frontier change.
scope_change_reason: The revision-8 card asks for one changed decoder or coframe itinerary on the selected supplier. This package instead prices the uncovered independent chart-pair grammar of the retained 640-input center-contact graph from PR #4867. That graph is not the selected P104 word. The result is a scoped obstruction for that grammar, not a supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: A mixed pair of retained-center contact charts cannot reduce the paid Gaussian moment; every such pair strictly increases it. That removes this chart grammar as a route to a larger-rank child at those contacts.
stop_rule: Stop after the complete pair census and the edgeless-set corollary. Do not enumerate mixed labels on a connected triple, rebuild the coherent-block flow, or search native words.
